Environmental-shift null (N2)

Source: R/nulls.R
dn_null_shift.Rd

Null distribution of directional coverage obtained by translating the species' coverage-weight array to random, availability-weighted positions in environmental space. Translation permutes lattice cells without altering density values, so the envelope of a shifted niche is exactly the shifted envelope; the weights are computed once and rolled.

Usage

dn_null_shift(
  Z_sp,
  Ze,
  Z_global,
  q = 0.95,
  B = 499L,
  statistic = c("auc", "q"),
  targets = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

Z_sp

R x R species density.

Ze

(k x P) region densities.

Z_global

R x R global availability density; shift targets are drawn proportional to it.

q

envelope level.

B

number of replicates (default 499).

statistic

"q" or "auc".

targets

optional integer vector of length B giving flat target cell indices (1-based, column-major on the R x R lattice); supply to reproduce a specific draw exactly (e.g. from the Python pipeline).

seed

RNG seed used when targets is NULL.

Value

(k x B) matrix of null coverage values.

Examples

set.seed(1)
bg <- cbind(rnorm(4000), rnorm(4000))
sp <- dn_space(bg, R = 50)
Zg <- dn_density(bg, sp)
Zs <- dn_density(cbind(rnorm(300, 1, 0.4), rnorm(300, 0, 0.4)), sp)
Ze <- matrix(as.numeric(dn_density(cbind(rnorm(300, 1, 0.3),
                                         rnorm(300, 0, 0.3)), sp)), 1)
obs <- as.numeric(Ze %*% dn_weights(Zs))
nul <- dn_null_shift(Zs, Ze, Zg, B = 99, seed = 1)
dn_null_summary(obs, nul)
#>    null_mean   null_sd      ses p_emp n_valid
#> 1 0.08130976 0.1325745 4.119742  0.01      99
